messages:
ops-bot: PAGER: continuous-batching latency spike detected on prod (region: us-west-2). 90th p90 tokens latency -> 9s, error rate +5%. Affected service: inference-runtime-batch. Auto-escalating to eng-oncall. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/5050012345 :rotating_light:

inc-bot: Incident created: CB-SAT-5050012345. Severity: high. Paging on-call. Runbook: continuous-batching -> step 1 (throttle ingress), step 2 (rollback recent batch config), step 3 (re-enable KV cache eviction).

ashley: I’m oncall and looking. Seeing queue depth spike on batch-controller pods 3/3. CPU not super high but per-pod queue latency huge.

sanjay: Confirming -- traces show microbatch sizes ballooning from ~4 -> ~120 tokens after the config push ~15m ago. Throughput per GPU steady but tail latency exploding.

lia: Which config was rolled? I see a rollout 14:52 that set `batching.window_ms` from 30 -> 10 and enabled `aggressive_prefetch=true` in the controller. Might be over-optimizing for tail.

kevin: I’m prepping a rollback for that rollout. Can we throttle front-door to reduce new inflight requests while we act?

maya: Throttling ingress to 50% for affected route now (`redwoodctl routes throttle --route /v1/generate --percent 50 --region us-west-2`).

ashley: Good. Throttle applied. Incoming QPS down ~45% and queue growth paused. Still lots of in-flight KV cache fills.

sre-lead: Noted customer impact: 3 paid customers on dedicated capacity in us-west-2 showing 5-10x p95 latency increases. Ops/Account notified?

maya: PagerDuty note sent to SEs for the affected customers, included mitigations and ETA.

kevin: Rollback initiated for batching-controller config to last stable (window_ms=30, aggressive_prefetch=false). Patch command:```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/batching-controller BATCH_WINDOW_MS=30 AGGRESSIVE_PREFETCH=false
```Applying now.

lia: Watching rollout. One replica failed readiness for ~30s but then recovered. Current controller pods show old env.

sanjay: After rollback, microbatch sizes back to ~6-8 on new requests. But KV cache has a backlog of large prefixes from the last 20m; eviction rates low and memory pressure high on 2 nodes.

ashley: We should rotate KV eviction policy to force more aggressive reclamation to avoid cascade. Proposing `kv_cache.eviction_threshold=0.6` from 0.8 for the cluster. Thoughts?

kevin: Agreed. I’ll patch live with caution. Command:```bash
kubectl exec -n inference -c controller batching-controller-0 -- /bin/sh -c "redwoodctl config set kv_cache.eviction_threshold 0.6 && redwoodctl config reload"
```Applying to one pod first.

maya: Patch applied to one pod; eviction started, memory freed. Rolling to others. Monitor delays in flight.

inc-bot: Note: rolling change to kv eviction may increase cache misses and per-token cost temporarily. Documenting in incident log.

ashley: After both rollback and eviction tweak, p95 dropped from ~6.2s -> 1.1s over 6 minutes. Error rate trending down. Queue depth back to baseline.

sre-lead: Great. Next: we need to run a controlled canary for the original optimization and add safety limits. Do NOT re-enable `aggressive_prefetch` until we add concurrency guard.

lia: Agreed. Proposed guard: only enable aggressive_prefetch when average concurrency per pod < 40 and queue depth < 10. Also cap the max microbatch size at 48 tokens.

kevin: I’ll prepare a hotfix branch with those checks in the controller (feature gate + telemetry). Quick patch snippet:```go
if cfg.AggressivePrefetch && metrics.Concurrency > cfg.PrefetchConcurrencyLimit {
    log.Warn("prefetch suppressed due to high concurrency")
    enabled = false
}
```
I can push to canary tomorrow.

maya: For customers: SE message drafted. We should offer to re-route critical traffic to dedicated fallback models or spin extra capacity for them if they need.

ashley: Post-incident checklist:
- incident timeline (assign: ashley)
- reproduce in staging with congestion harness (assign: sanjay)
- permanent guard rails + unit tests (assign: kevin)
- update runbook with prefetch safety limits (assign: lia)
- customer comms + RCA (assign: maya)

sre-lead: Also create an alert for sudden microbatch growth: trigger when median->90th microbatch size ratio > 5 within 5m. Add tagging to correlate with recent config rollouts.

inc-bot: Incident CB-SAT-5050012345 severity reduced to medium. Remediation in progress. ETA for full RCA: 72h.

ashley: Closing live mitigation loop. Will remain in thread for follow-ups. Thanks all — great coordination. :thumbsup:
